parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence (sodomy law struck down 2023), no documented universal-exposure measure (no facility, border, custody or ward rule stated), and no police or state targeting of trans people. Positives are documented: police protected Pride, PM-backed sit-in, religious leaders condemning counter-protest, welcoming resorts, polls placing the country among the region's more LGBTQ-friendly, HRT in public hospitals. Negatives are societal, not institutional: 2024 election hate speech, 2018 Pride death threats (event-scoped, with state protection around it), one dated 2016 harassment incident, pervasive stigmatisation, no gender-identity discrimination cover, no legal gender recognition — a resident gap, not visitor exposure. Border markers, custody placement and emergency-care treatment of outed visitors are open questions, not exposures. Worst feature is tier 3-4 societal hostility with functioning state actors partially protective; no organised trans-specific targeting. Thin trans data pulls slightly below the 0.65 anchors.
